[[File:Spellbook (DSII).jpg|thumb|Example of a Spellbook screen in {{Dungeon Siege II}}]]
{{For|2=Spells}}

'''Spells''' in {{Dungeon Siege II}} haven't changed much since the original {{Dungeon Siege}} game. Magic is still divided into two schools: nature and combat. To use your spells, you need a spell book, which now contains:
* 4 active spells.
* 2 auto spells (4 in {{Broken World}}). Here you can add only spells to heal and strengthen allies, as well as curse enemies and summon creatures.
* 4 spares (2 in BW).
The total number of spells has been reduced, but instead some enchantments have been tiered, allowing the same enchantments to be used later in the game.

Also, due to the addition of passive skills to each [[Classes (Dungeon Siege II)|class]] the effectiveness of the spells themselves has increased - mages can increase their damage and spell speed, increase their overall effectiveness and reduce mana costs. The functions of wizards in the squad have become even more pronounced: [[Nature Mage (Dungeon Siege II)|Nature Mages]] can (in addition to dealing damage) heal, buff and protect the squad, while [[Combat Mage (Dungeon Siege II)|combat]] - weaken and quickly destroy enemies. 

The summoned creatures of the school of nature have a lot of health and fight in close combat, and those of combat magic have good damage and a long-range attack type.

In the {{Broken World}} expansion, the [[Blood Assassin]] and [[Stone Fist]] skill trees added special buff spells that work like normal buffs and allow you to distribute experience between two classes in a ratio of 70/30, where 70 % - melee or ranged combat, 30% - natural or combat magic.

=Classes=
There are further specializations within each class, and so also in the magic classes. For example, a Nature Mage might specialize in Summoning or Ice Magic, among others, and might therefore be very different in between.

Like the original game, nature magic focuses on hurting your enemy and helping your teammates. You'll find most healing spells and buffs (performace-boosting spells) here. Combat Magic on the other hand is more about hurting and hindering your enemies.

Apart from the Nature and Combat magic classes, the spells themselves are also split into various elements. Some enemies have weaknesses to some elements, while others may be completely immune to it. It's wise to always keep a varied spellbook for such occasions.

Spells are devided in different classes, see below:

* [[Spells (Dungeon Siege II)#Death Spells|<span style="color:#C69030;">'''Death:'''</span>]] Death Magic can be found in the Combat Magic class and attacks the creatures lifeforce.
* [[Spells (Dungeon Siege II)#Fire Spells|<span style="color:#C69030;">'''Fire:'''</span>]] Fire Magic is also a favourite of Combat Magicians and deals with all things hot and burning. If you like spells that hit a lot of enemies at once, Fire Magic's your class.
* [[Spells (Dungeon Siege II)#Lightning Spells|<span style="color:#C69030;">'''Lightning:'''</span>]] A Combat Magician casting lots of Lightning spells generally don't do as much damage per hit, but they'll fire faster and cost less mana.
* [[Spells (Dungeon Siege II)#Curses|<span style="color:#C69030;">'''Curses:'''</span>]] A Combat Magician specialising in cursing will weaken the enemy so that it's easier to kill.
* [[Spells (Dungeon Siege II)#Offensive Spells|<span style="color:#41AA60;">'''Ice:'''</span>]] A Nature Magician specialising in Ice Magic can summon shards of ice out of thin air to hit the enemy with. Ice magic can also slow enemies down or freeze them instantly.
* [[Spells (Dungeon Siege II)#Healing Spells|<span style="color:#41AA60;">'''Healing:'''</span>]] A Nature Magicians best friend are their healing spells. Ranging from a quick one time boost, to more hitpoints gradually over time, healing spells will make sure your party members stay alive.
* [[Spells (Dungeon Siege II)#Summoning Spells|<span style="color:#41AA60;">'''Summoning:'''</span>]] Though both Combat and Nature magicians can summon creatures to aid their cause, Nature Magicians will find themselves much better at it.
* [[Spells (Dungeon Siege II)#Wrath Spells|<span style="color:#41AA60;">'''Buffing:'''</span>]] Those spells designed to temporarily boost a party member's attributes are called Buffs. A Nature Mage specialising in buffs can help parties win against even the toughest foes.
{{Clr}}

=Trivia=
*The additional shooting damage from Mana Shot depends not only on the skill "Enchanted Weapon" in the Blood Assassin tree, but also on the "Sharp Arrow" in the Archer tree. If the "Mana Shot" says +50 to shooting damage, and the damage bonus from Sharp Arrow is +50%, then in fact "Mana Shot" will add +75 to shooting damage. "Mana Strike" works similarly with the "Suppression" skill in the melee branch.
